surfaces: standards/SPIFFE_ID_and_SVID.md or current canonical SPIFFE Identity/SVID specification
local Workload API and SVID issuance/rotation

source_findings: SPIFFE separates a structured workload identity namespace (SPIFFE ID), a cryptographically verifiable identity document (SVID), and a runtime API used to obtain/refresh identities.

The SPIFFE Workload Endpoint is intended to be local to one host for bootstrap/security reasons; caller identity is normally established out-of-band from local process/OS properties rather than by trusting caller-supplied identity claims.
X.509-SVIDs support short-lived workload identity and mutual TLS; trust bundles can rotate and the Workload API streams updated X.509 identities/bundles.

JWT-SVIDs are bearer tokens with an inherent replay window; audience and expiration reduce but do not eliminate replay risk, so X.509 identity is the stronger default comparator for the F2 optional bridge.
SPIFFE trust domains bind an identity namespace to an issuing authority and cryptographic bundle; multiple keys support rotation while preserving namespace identity.

SPIRE implements the standard with a server plus one or more agents, registration entries, node attestation and workload attestation. This is a materially larger operational surface than F2-WP-1106 currently requires for one optional owner-controlled bridge.

SPIRE workload attestation can bind identities to OS/process attributes such as uid/gid/systemd properties or container/orchestrator selectors; this is useful as a design comparator for local runtime identity evidence.

SPIFFE/SPIRE identity authenticates a peer/workload; it does not by itself establish F2 canonical state lineage, capability authority, effect authority or semantic truth. Those remain separate F2 invariants.

thin_native_candidate_rules: Keep a stable typed bridge peer namespace/peer identity separate from transport address and from canonical local state identity.
Bind authenticated peer identity to short-lived credential evidence, issuer/trust-root fingerprint, validity interval and rotation generation.
Prefer mutual-authenticated channel identity for the optional bridge over reusable bearer identity tokens.
Bind any remote capability declaration separately to the authenticated peer identity, protocol version and exact local state-lineage digest; authenticated identity must never self-grant capabilities.
Fail closed on unknown issuer/root, expired credential, unexpected peer identity, capability mismatch, lineage mismatch or stale credential generation.
Preserve local boot/state continuity when no bridge identity can be established; unavailable/invalid remote identity must degrade to detached local operation, not block baseline local boot.
Treat remote returns as candidate/projection evidence only even after successful peer authentication.

counterhypothesis: Even the distilled SPIFFE-inspired namespace/SVID abstraction may be unnecessary. A single pinned endpoint public key plus direct mTLS, an explicit capability manifest and F2 state-lineage/session binding may provide equivalent assurance with less code and fewer moving parts.
next_falsifier: Map the SPIFFE-derived invariants directly onto the current F2-WP-1106 data model and compare three designs: A) raw pinned-key/mTLS, B) thin SPIFFE-inspired BridgePeerIdentity + rotating credential/capability envelope, C) full SPIRE. Score state/effect authority separation, replay/rotation handling, failure isolation, implementation/dependency weight and testability. Promote only if B adds a concrete invariant that A lacks without importing C's control-plane cost.
